image_description: Two male ducks (drakes) floating on rippled water. The duck in the foreground (left) has a dark green iridescent head, white neck ring, and grey body, consistent with a Mallard. The duck in the background (right) has a black head, white breast, and grey flanks, resembling a Common Merganser or similar species. Both are swimming calmly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreground duck has a yellowish bill, but the background duck has a long, thin, pointed red/orange bill (typical of a merganser), which contradicts the 'broad, flat' description provided in the generic drake taxonomy. Additionally, the foreground bill appears somewhat short and lacks the distinct lamellae texture expected of a filter-feeder.
Both visible eyes appear dark and correctly positioned on the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both subjects exhibit streamlined, buoyant bodies sitting low in the water with plausible plumage density.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreground duck matches the Mallard description perfectly (green head, white ring). The background duck shows distinct breeding plumage (black/white/grey), fitting the general 'colorful/distinct' criteria even if it's a different species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely submerged underwater and not visible in the image.
The folded wings on both ducks appear structurally sound, broad, and tapered correctly against the body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreground duck displays the characteristic curled central tail feathers. The background duck's tail is less distinct but appears short and appropriate.
